That supplier requires an integrable unbiased random variable at each fixed parameter, but no jointly measurable oracle realization or measurable probability kernel. These conditions do not ensure that the random-parameter calls, hence the returned estimator, are measurable. For example, take Θ = R, H = J = 0, θ = 0, c = 1, Δ uniform on [-2,-1] ∪ [1,2], and an independent centered Rademacher simulator input Z. For a non-Lebesgue-measurable A ⊂ [1,2], define the oracle family Y(η,Z) = 1_A(η)Z. Every fixed-η call is integrable and unbiased, and all algorithm input conditions hold. With shared Z, the returned output is (1_A(Δ) − 1_A(−Δ))Z/(2Δ), whose nonzero event is {Δ ∈ A ∪ (−A)}, which is not measurable. The algorithm therefore needs an explicit measurability condition on random-parameter oracle calls or on the oracle realization. The moment theorems separately assume conditional expectations of their outputs and are not refuted by this example.

row.reason: The assumptions make every denominator nonzero and both query points admissible almost surely; the procedure then makes exactly two oracle calls and defines all coordinates from their shared difference. No unbiasedness or convergence claim is made.
